Simulated Ohio forest-pond SNP and microsatellite data

Source: R/ohio_ponds_data.R
ohio_ponds.Rd

Matched SNP and microsatellite genotypes for 20 retained diploid animals in each of 24 hypothetical forest ponds on a real southeastern Ohio landscape. The neutral SLiM simulation was motivated by a forest pond-breeding salamander. Pond locations, hydroperiods, demographic parameters, and genetic data are simulated. Elevation and land cover are derived from public USGS products.

Usage

data(ohio_ponds)

Format

A list with 12 elements:

covariates

A packed terra::SpatRaster with 102 rows and 102 columns at 100 m resolution in NAD83 / UTM zone 17N (EPSG:26917). Layers are forest (fraction from 0 to 1), slope (degrees), and elevation (meters).

forest500

A packed raster on the same grid containing forest fraction smoothed with a Gaussian kernel of standard deviation 500 m. This is the context layer used to generate pond exchange.

ponds

A 24-row data frame in population order. pond is the identifier; x and y are UTM coordinates in meters; cell is the 100 m raster cell; slope is in degrees; edge_m is distance to the domain edge in meters; forest_buffer_100m, forest_buffer_300m, and forest_buffer_500m are cell-center forest fractions in circular buffers of the indicated radius. hydroperiod is a hypothetical pond covariate in days with no simulated genetic effect; nlcd_30m is the native land-cover code at the pond; displacement_from_trace25_m and candidate_count_at_selection record the location-screening procedure; focal flags a sampled pond; fold gives three spatial validation blocks.

samples

A 480-row data frame in genotype row order. individual and pond are identifiers; population is the one-based pond index; pedigree_id, parent_1, and parent_2 are SLiM pedigree identifiers (-1 denotes an unavailable parent); x and y are the pond coordinates.

raw_samples

The same columns for 780 initial and additional captures before pedigree screening. Sampling began with 30 per pond, with additional captures where necessary to retain 20.

snp

A 480 by 2500 integer matrix of alternate-allele dosage (0, 1, or 2), with individual row names and locus column names.

raw_snp

A 780 by 2500 dosage matrix for the raw captures, using exactly the same loci as snp.

snp_positions

The 2500 SNP positions in base pairs along a 50 Mb simulated chromosome, in column order.

microsat

A 480 by 48 integer matrix of repeat counts at 24 stepwise-mutation loci. Adjacent columns hold the two alleles at one locus. Row names match snp; values are repeat counts, not dosage.

raw_microsat

A 780 by 48 matrix for the raw captures at the same microsatellite loci.

microsat_loci

A length-48 character vector assigning each microsatellite allele column to its locus.

simulation

A named list recording simulation and mutation seeds, the 1200 compressed generations, demographic and marker parameters, the known 500 m forest context, the raw log-conductance coefficient of 6, the maximum pond-exchange probability of 0.025, the null hydroperiod effect, and the assumptions used in the teaching analyses.

Source

USGS 3D Elevation Program and USGS Annual National Land Cover Database 2023 (Collection 1.0), processed to a common projected grid. Source URLs, hashes, processing, and simulation provenance are recorded in system.file("extdata", "ohio-ponds", "PROVENANCE.md", package = "terradish").

Details

Call terra::unwrap() on the two packed raster elements before use. No downloads or simulation software are needed to analyze the bundled data. All retained individuals have both marker panels from the same ancestry. Screening removes known immediate pedigree relationships within ponds; this is not a claim that the retained animals are unrelated at deeper generations or that such relationships would be known in field samples.

Ponds were screened for native forest, at least 90 percent forest within 100 m, and at least 60 percent within 300 m. These are hypothetical design rules, not estimated habitat thresholds. Exchange has strong reproductive philopatry with a long tail among ponds. The exchange model uses endpoints on a resistance graph; it does not simulate observed animal travel paths.

The SNP panel was filtered for pooled retained-sample minor allele frequency of at least 0.05. Locus spacing does not establish independent loci. The effective degrees of freedom used in a Wishart example is an assumption, distinct from the SNP count. Spatial validation conditions on this globally ascertained panel, rather than validating marker discovery itself.

The source history was specified before fitting. Other histories and SNP panel sizes were checked during development; the bundled history was not selected for the strongest fit. The simulation illustrates an estimable mechanism, not calibration or validation of a species-specific demographic model. See the installed provenance file for sources and processing details.

Examples

data(ohio_ponds)
covariates <- terra::unwrap(ohio_ponds$covariates)
dim(ohio_ponds$snp)       # individuals by SNPs
#> [1]  480 2500
dim(ohio_ponds$microsat)  # individuals by two allele columns per locus
#> [1] 480  48
table(ohio_ponds$samples$pond)
#> 
#> P01 P02 P03 P04 P05 P06 P07 P08 P09 P10 P11 P12 P13 P14 P15 P16 P17 P18 P19 P20 
#>  20  20  20  20  20  20  20  20  20  20  20  20  20  20  20  20  20  20  20  20 
#> P21 P22 P23 P24 
#>  20  20  20  20 
terra::res(covariates)   # map units are meters
#> [1] 100 100

# Aggregate diploid dosage to counts of alternate alleles in each pond.
groups <- factor(ohio_ponds$samples$pond, levels = ohio_ponds$ponds$pond)
Y <- rowsum(ohio_ponds$snp, groups, reorder = FALSE)
Y <- Y[ohio_ponds$ponds$pond, , drop = FALSE]
N <- 2 * as.numeric(table(groups))
S <- cov_from_biallelic(Y, N) / N[1]
round(S[1:4, 1:4], 3)
#>        P01   P02   P03    P04
#> P01  0.336 0.053 0.025 -0.015
#> P02  0.053 0.260 0.067  0.031
#> P03  0.025 0.067 0.156  0.031
#> P04 -0.015 0.031 0.031  0.293
